messages:
alex.s: Heads-up — I'm proposing audit schema v3 to support RBAC scopes and KMS key id. Main changes: replace flat actor_* fields with an `actor` object (id,type,identifiers), add `kms_key_id`, and remove the legacy `session_id` field. Need migration plan + customer-facing validation.
priya.k: +1. Can you paste a minimal example of old vs new event?
alex.s: Sure:
```json
// v2
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-15T12:01:02Z",
  "actor_email": "alice@acme.com",
  "action": "file.download",
  "resource": "/models/567",
  "session_id": "abcd1234"
}
// v3
{
  "ts": "2026-03-15T12:01:02Z",
  "actor": {"id":"usr_123","type":"user","identifiers":["alice@acme.com"]},
  "action":"file.download",
  "resource":"/models/567",
  "kms_key_id":"projects/redwood/keys/infra-xyz",
  "audit_version":"v3"
}
```
carlos_r: Removing `session_id` ok? some infra pipelines use it for tracing across services.
emily-w: We use `session_id` in a few customer-facing integrations (Splunk/Datadog). If we drop it we must emit a derived `trace_id` or keep compat field as `legacy_session` for one release cycle.
alex.s: Good catch — plan: keep `legacy_session` for ~6 weeks while we migrate ingestors, then drop. We'll include server-side mapping to populate `legacy_session` from `actor.identifiers[0]` if present.
mike.dev: How does `kms_key_id` affect PII export controls? Security wants proof that `kms_key_id` maps to customer-managed key only for Private deployments.
priya.k: For Hosted, `kms_key_id` will be null unless customer requested CSMK. We should validate at ingest: if `kms_key_id` present and `deployment_type` != private -> reject with 400 + guidance link.
audit-bot: NOTE: schema tool (audit-lint) can validate v2/v3 and emit diffs — https://go/audit-lint
emily-w: Migration checklist suggestion:
- add v3 producer flag behind feature flag
- emit both v2 & v3 simultaneously for 2 weeks
- roll ingesters to accept either format
- run historical reindex for analytics
- remove `legacy_session` after opt-out window
priya.k: Also need customer-facing validator: endpoint that returns sample events and validation errors. Product will want it for support cases.
alex.s: I'll draft the short public doc blurb: "audit events now include standardized actor object and optional kms_key_id; we guarantee dual-writing for 2 weeks; contact support to opt into CSMK validations." Thoughts?
carlos_r: Add note about RBAC: `actor.type` can be `service`/`bot`/`org-admin`, and we should expose `actor.roles` only in internal audit records, never in customer-facing events.
mike.dev: Ops ask: can we version events via top-level `audit_version` and keep `event_id` stable? That makes routing simpler.
alex.s: Yes — `audit_version` top-level string. Event IDs stay UUIDv4. We'll bump our schema registry and tag ingestion rules.
priya.k: Timeline proposal: feature flag on staging this week, dual-write alpha next week, public dual-write roll 2w, deprecation notice 4w after roll. Any blockers?
emily-w: Need SE/Docs to prepare migration guide and sample parsers for Splunk/Datadog.
alex.s: I'll ping @docs and @se. @audit-bot can we run a quick compatibility sweep across downstream consumers? :pray:
audit-bot: Scheduling compatibility sweep job now — expected results in ~2h.
carlos_r: One more: tests — add schema fuzz tests and ingest smoke test that validates RBAC-scoped events produce correct `actor.roles` internal-only filtering.
priya.k: I'll own the migration task list. I'll create a checklist in GH and link here when done.
alex.s: Thanks — I'll open the PR for schema change + linting rule. Will tag folks for review.
mike.dev: ack. schedule a short sync if audit-bot finds >0 incompatible consumers.
alex.s: SG. Thanks all :thumbsup:
